title: Run-Length Encoding
statement:
Compress a string by replacing each run of identical characters with the character followed by the run length.

## Your function

```
std::string RunLengthEncode(const std::string& text);
```

`"aaabcc"` becomes `"a3b1c2"`. A single character still gets its count (`"b1"`), so the encoding is unambiguous. The empty string encodes to the empty string. The input contains no digits.

## Watch out

- **The last run is never followed by a different character,** so a loop that writes a run only when the character changes forgets it. Flush after the loop.
- **Counts can have several digits.** A run of 12 is `"a12"`: build the count with `std::to_string`, not by adding to a `char`.
- **Do not read `text[0]` when `text` is empty.**

tests.name: the final run must be flushed
a run of twelve has a two-digit count
